@graph.name: Port of Baltimore Logistics Dataset
@graph.description: The per-port dataset for the Port of Baltimore in the Ports & Intermodal program of The Flat Rate Movers: the full port record for the Helen Delich Bentley Port of Baltimore — the public terminals owned by the State of Maryland and managed by the Maryland Port Administration (MDOT MPA), with Seagirt Marine Terminal operated by Ports America Chesapeake under a 50-year public-private partnership from 2010 — its terminals (Seagirt Marine Terminal, 4 berths at 50 ft with 1.5M TEU/yr capacity; the Intermodal Container Transfer Facility, CSX Intermodal, on-dock at Seagirt; Dundalk Marine Terminal, 570 acres; North and South Locust Point; and the Fairfield / Masonville auto and RoRo complex), the port's container volume and cargo rankings on the Maryland Port Administration's named bases (1,113,309 TEU in CY2025, a port record; the highest RoRo farm and construction equipment tonnage of any U.S. port, 887,513 short tons in CY2025; first among U.S. ports for forest products, 1.1M short tons in CY2025; second in the U.S. for autos and light trucks, 728,225 units in CY2025), on-dock CSX service at the ICTF with Norfolk Southern serving the port via interchange and the Canton Railroad, the I-95, I-695, I-70, I-83 and I-81 corridors, and the branch binding: the port is served from the Martinsburg, WV branch, about 91-96 road miles away (Winchester measures 106-116). The company's eight attached port services are recorded cell by cell in the companion coverage dataset. No port tenancy or port-authority relationship is claimed; the company's crews hold TWIC cards and its contractors hold valid TWIC cards.

@graph.name: Port of Baltimore Service Coverage Dataset
@graph.description: The service-coverage cells for the Port of Baltimore in the Ports & Intermodal program: the eight attached services (transloading; ocean container packing and unpacking; loading and unloading / container labor; cross-docking; freight rework; specialized workforce; logistics project management; 3PL support services), each recorded as offered with its delivery points (port-adjacent warehouse, receiver's dock, yard, leased space, and on-terminal by arrangement — on-terminal work happens only by arrangement through the terminal's own processes, never as a bare claim) and its bound branch, Martinsburg, WV. Drayage is not offered at any port in the program.

@graph.name: Helen Delich Bentley Port of Baltimore
@graph.description: Helen Delich Bentley Port of Baltimore (Baltimore, MD) — deepwater marine port (containers, RoRo, autos, forest products, breakbulk). Authority: Maryland Port Administration (MDOT MPA). Operator: Maryland Port Administration (public terminals are state-owned and MPA-managed; Seagirt is operated by Ports America Chesapeake under a 50-year public-private partnership from 2010). Cargo: containers (Seagirt); RoRo farm and construction equipment — highest tonnage of any U.S. port (887,513 tons, 2025); forest products — first among U.S. ports (1.1M tons, 2025); autos and light trucks — second in the U.S. (728,225 units, 2025). Rail: CSX — on-dock at the ICTF adjacent to Seagirt (CSX Intermodal); CSX direct to all North Locust Point berths; Norfolk Southern — serves the port via interchange / Canton Railroad — not an on-dock Seagirt operator. Highway corridors: I-95, I-695, I-70, I-83, I-81. Volume (CY2025, calendar): 1,113,309 TEU — Port of Baltimore containers — a port record (source: Maryland Port Administration 2025 results release, 2026-03-24). Volume (CY2025, calendar): 887,513 short tons — RoRo farm and construction equipment — highest of any U.S. port (source: Maryland Port Administration 2025 results release, 2026-03-24). Volume (CY2025, calendar): 1,100,000 short tons — Forest products — first among U.S. ports (published as 1.1M tons) (source: Maryland Port Administration 2025 results release, 2026-03-24). Volume (CY2025, calendar): 728,225 units — Autos and light trucks — second in the U.S. (source: Maryland Port Administration 2025 results release, 2026-03-24). Branch binding: this port is served from the Martinsburg, WV branch of The Flat Rate Movers — about 106-116 road miles from Winchester and 91-96 from Martinsburg; bound to Martinsburg on miles. modest margin, about 12-18 mi; Winchester is a credible support branch.
